_comment: SzpontNet's own network model - the canonical v1 constants tabulated in szpontnet/docs/appendix-b-constants.md. A node with no host behind it runs on exactly this. A host (see host.py) may return an overlay from Host.model(); it is merged one level deep over these, so a deployment can restate the duty catalog, retune a protocol constant or relabel the tiers without forking the library. Nothing here is presentational: titles, emoji and colours belong to whoever renders a node, not to the protocol.

protocol._comment: Discovery is UDP (multicast + subnet broadcast, receivers dedupe - Wi-Fi APs commonly drop multicast); links are TCP with NDJSON messages. A node is 'stale' after missing heartbeats for peerStaleSecs and 'down' (duties reassigned) after peerTimeoutSecs.

accounts._comment: Subscription plans and the accounting knobs behind per-node load balancing. A plan's 'weight' is its quota capacity RELATIVE to Pro (Max 5× → 5, Max 20× → 20); capacity units = weight × capacityPerWeight. Absolute token quotas are intentionally NOT hard-coded - the provider's limits are dynamic rolling windows. usageAvg is an exponential rolling average of consumption with a ~21-day time constant; quotaLeft is remaining capacity in the current window. Both are retained for display and for peers on older builds; routing ranks on 'surplus' instead (see _surplusComment).
accounts._surplusComment: A node's surplus is a burn-down RATIO, not an amount: the budget left in its quota window divided by the share of that window's clock still ahead of it. 1.0 is exactly on pace, above is flush, below is rationing. Measuring it relatively is the entire point - 60% left with 2 of 7 days to go paces at 2.1 (that budget expires at the reset, so spend it here), while 70% left with 6 of 7 days to go paces at 0.82 (genuinely low, despite the bigger number). Ranking on the raw remaining amount gets both cases backwards: it hoards the account that is about to reset and drains the one that has to stretch. Each node computes its own surplus from the real reset instants its usage endpoint reports for the 5-hour session and 7-day week windows (the tighter of the two binds), falling back to pacing its local bookkeeping window when the probe is unavailable. Capped at 10.0, since past that a node is simply 'use it or lose it'.
accounts._tokenComment: Automatic token-budget signal (the ok/low/out state a UI shows and the mesh routes around). PRIMARY: the node probes the account's REAL remaining quota via the OAuth usage endpoint - utilization of the 5-hour session and 7-day week rate-limit windows, gossiped as tokensSessionPct/tokensWeekPct; the binding (smaller) fraction drives the state: ≥ lowThreshold → ok, > 0 → low, ≤ 0 → out. FALLBACK (no credentials / offline / SZPONTNET_OAUTH_PROBE=0): the node measures its OWN recent consumption from the local agent logs over the last usageWindowHours against a heuristic per-plan ceiling = plan.weight × tokensPerWeight. The fallback is deliberately rough (real limits are dynamic and account-specific) - the UIs mark it '≈'; tune tokensPerWeight, or pin a node's state with the manual override.

tiers._comment: Machine strength, 1 = strongest. 'weakest-first' keeps the strong machine free for interactive work by routing grunt jobs to the weakest eligible node. Auto-detected CPU-quality-first (Apple-Silicon variant / boost clock, then physical cores, RAM, dGPU - see hardware.py); a manual edit pins it. 'labels' give a UI human words instead of a bare number.

trust._comment: The trust level applied to an UNKNOWN device - one whose proven fingerprint is not in this node's local allowlist. Ships 'foreign' (zero-trust): a new device is untrusted until the operator promotes it. Set to 'personal' for the full-altruism mode where every unlisted peer is trusted. The trust VOCABULARY a UI renders (titles, colours) is not the protocol's business and lives with whoever renders it.

duties._comment: The bundle E2E runs on one Linux AND one macOS node - platform coverage beats machine preference here. No 'strategy' key, so it inherits defaultStrategy (surplus-first): within each platform slot the flusher node wins.
